<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-print`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-print/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/plugins/development.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/ui/print-pages.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/print/records (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in handlePrintRecord))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-print/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `97c160b65ebc105e8f484700fe6c88081e107428` — the merge of head `3dfbfdb5a135338fd76d80ceab81442c2315d4df` into base `057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 97c160b65ebc105e8f484700fe6c88081e107428 && git checkout 97c160b65ebc105e8f484700fe6c88081e107428
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65 3dfbfdb5a135338fd76d80ceab81442c2315d4df && git checkout -B drift-repro 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65 && git merge --no-ff 3dfbfdb5a135338fd76d80ceab81442c2315d4df

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · L1 · head `3dfbfdb5a135338fd76d80ceab81442c2315d4df` · 2026-11-25T10:59Z

- **Shape (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37272`, CLEAN, 13 items):** open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #37260`, no closing keyword on another card, no `content/docs/releases/` path, a changeset for each published package touched (`@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-print`, both `patch`), no `+0/-0` file, declarations `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset. `Fixes` is right. The card's Expected (the 503/504/500 sentences translated by the request locale, toast in the UI language) is delivered whole. The two English sentences outside the card (the `/actions` 503 and the bridge 501) are on #37273.
- **Seat direction A is followed** (7159533198, 2026-11-25T10:18Z). Both call sites pass the localized text as `sendServerFault`'s `message` argument (`print-routes.ts`: the caller-resolution arm and `relayPrintFailure`). No `userMessage` and no `declaredCode` are added on a 5xx. `sendServerFault`'s signature and envelope are untouched. This matches the docblock in `packages/types/src/response-envelope.ts` ("The wire carries `message`, the route's generic text, and nothing of `thrown`") and the actions-door fault exit in `actions-door-answer.ts` (~L311: "a fault's `userMessage` … do[es] not ride this exit"). The thrown value still reaches only the fault log.
- **Clause-② holds (`no`).** The only spec edit adds 16 string entries under the existing `en`/`zh-CN`/`ja-JP`/`es-ES` objects of `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES`, plus TSDoc. There is no new export and no type change:
  - The declaring line `export const BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES: Record…` (string-keyed `Record` of string-keyed `Record`s of `string`) is an unchanged context line in the diff. Its key type is explicitly `string`, not a literal union inferred from the object, so a new key cannot reach the `.d.ts`.
  - Named probe, built at head: `packages/spec/dist` carries `declare const BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` with that same string-keyed nested `Record` type.
  - No type in the tree derives from the catalog's keys: `git grep "typeof BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES"` finds nothing in `packages/`.
  - `serverAnswerKeyFor`'s literal return type is module-private in service-print.
  - The two other consumers (`core/src/utils/operation-user-message.ts` and `plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`) read only locale presence through `resolveBundleLocale`. More keys do not change what they do.
- **English is byte-identical.** I extracted the four literals from `print-routes.ts` at merge-base `9171bed0a65` and compared them as `Buffer`s with `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES.en[k]` from the head build. All four are BYTE-EQUAL (`print_caller_unresolved`, `print_engine_unavailable`, `print_timed_out`, `print_failed`). The control pin "the English sentences are the ones the door answered before they were localized" passes at head.
- **Pins re-run at head** in a throwaway worktree, after building spec and service-print's dependency closure: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-print exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/print-routes.test.ts` gives `Tests 36 passed (36)`. All 10 pins under "its own 5xx sentences, in the request's language" are ✓. Catalog suite: `vitest run src/system/operation-message.test.ts` gives `60 passed (60)`.
- **Ablation reproduced (4 red).** I ran `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with the anchor `return operationUserMessage(serverAnswerKeyFor(status), { locale });` replaced by the three original English returns. The mutation landed (blob `44b2c38dcc4e` → `f01bdac1104e`). The result was `Tests 4 failed | 32 passed (36)`: the three zh-CN pins (503/504/500) and the ja→ja-JP pin. The English controls stayed green, and the restore was verified (`git diff HEAD` empty).
  - The author's ablation does not exercise the caller-resolution arm, so I added a second ablation of `operationUserMessage('print_caller_unresolved', …)` → the English literal. It gives `1 failed | 35 passed`, and only the caller-resolution pin is red.
- **Fallback to English holds.** I probed `preferredLocaleFromHeader` → `operationUserMessage('print_failed', …)` on the head build:
  - absent, `""`, `*`, `en-US,en;q=0.9`, `de-DE`, `xx` and `fr-FR,zh-CN;q=0.9` all return the English sentence. Only the top tag is read, by design, the same reading the platform uses elsewhere.
  - `zh`, `ZH-cn`, `ja` and `es-MX` reach their catalogs.
  - Observation, not graded: `zh-TW` renders the Simplified zh-CN text. That is existing `resolveBundleLocale` base matching and was not changed here.
- **Benefit past the boundary, checked by reading the code (no browser run):**
  - The console sets `Accept-Language` on API calls (`ui/packages/auth/src/createAuthenticatedFetch.ts:146–149`).
  - `/actions` forwards it: `'accept-language'` is in `API_FORWARD_HEADER_ALLOWLIST`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:1451`.
  - `/actions` relays the target's `error.message` as written (`apiActionForwardRefusal`, `action-execution.ts:2448–2452`; `forward-refused`, `action-dispatch.ts:920–930`).
  - Browser reach stays NOT MEASURED, as the zone said.
- **Translation quality:** all twelve localized strings are accurate. None names a wire code, host or path. `zh-CN` and `ja-JP` match the catalog's polite register. `print_failed` and `print_caller_unresolved` read naturally in all three languages. N1–N3 below are phrasing nits only.
- **Bounded in-place fix (caller-resolution 500), four conditions met:** same defect class (the door's own hard-coded English 5xx), mechanical, nobody else claims it, same gate family and same file. The PR body names it and pins it.
- **Gates:**
  - Check-runs at `3dfbfdb5a1`: 58 `success`, 11 `skipped` (expected), 0 failed, 0 pending.
  - `Lint & Repo Gates`: `success`. `TypeScript Type Check`: `success`. `Test Core` (1–10/10): `success`.
  - `mergeable_state: clean`.
  - K = 2 (`landing-k.mjs --pr 37272`: PRBASE `057cedfa9b` → origin/main `f9fda2a4f8`). The locale leg has no new pack, and the shared-budget leg has no book.
  - `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 3dfbfdb5a` exits 0 (clean).
  - Main since the merge-base touches none of `service-print/`, `operation-message.ts` or `operation-user-message.ts`.
- **Changeset, read sentence by sentence (`.changeset/37260-print-failure-locale.md`):**
  - "now answers its own 5xx sentences in the request's language": true, and the route is `PRINT_RECORDS_ROUTE = '/api/v1/print/records'`.
  - "used to answer a fixed English `error.message` whatever the request's `Accept-Language`": true (merge-base `serverAnswerFor`).
  - "four keys … in `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES`, written through `operationUserMessage` … in the request's top `Accept-Language` tag": true.
  - "the `/actions` door forwards the caller's `Accept-Language` and relays the door's `message` as written": true (allowlist and `apiActionForwardRefusal`, above).
  - "Code, status and the English text do not change: … English, … no `Accept-Language`, or … a language the catalog carries no text for, reads the same sentence as before": true (byte check and fallback probe).
  - "What the engine or the host said is still withheld from the wire and kept in the server fault log": true, because `sendServerFault` is unchanged.
  - A `patch` level for new catalog keys matches the `spec` CHANGELOG's precedent (`record_not_found`, `query_field_not_readable` and `delegation_scope_violation` shipped as Patch).
- **维护者速读, read sentence by sentence:**
  - 用户能看到什么变化: true for the 503, 504 and fallback paths. English is unchanged, as checked above. It does not mention the fourth sentence, the caller-resolution 500 (N5).
  - 为什么做: matches the card's repro and its p1 reason.
  - 出错会怎样: true. Status and code are pinned unchanged in every new case through `envelope(answer)`, and the change touches no print logic. A revert is one commit.
  - 要你做什么：无: true. No governed path, and no maintainer decision is open.
- **Overlap:** I scanned the changed-file lists of all 41 open PRs. The only hit is the release PR #35129 (`changeset-release/main`), which touches only `service-print/CHANGELOG.md` and `package.json`. No open PR touches `print-routes.ts`, `operation-message.ts` or `operation-user-message.ts`.
- **Contract review:** `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths …` reads the schema face (hit `packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`), so a review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. A draft record is filed beside this one, served at `TIER_DEFAULT`, and the seat re-runs it at tier before landing. The zone comment's "no governed path" holds: the path is on no Prime Directive #14 surface. The contract review is owed by the schema face, not by governance.
- N1 — `zh-CN.print_timed_out` `记录未能在打印允许的时间内打印为文件。` is literal and stiff ("打印允许的时间"). Better: `打印超时：记录未能在允许的时间内打印为文件。`
- N2 — `ja-JP.print_engine_unavailable` stacks two negatives in two short sentences (`…印刷できません。印刷エンジンの準備ができていません。…`). Better: `印刷エンジンの準備ができていないため、現在レコードをファイルに印刷できません。原因はサーバーログに記録されています。` In `ja-JP.print_timed_out`, `印刷に許可された時間内に…` is stiff. Better: `制限時間内にレコードをファイルに印刷できませんでした。`
- N3 — Two phrasing points in `es-ES.print_engine_unavailable`:
  - `Ahora mismo` is colloquial next to the catalog's formal *usted* voice (`Póngase en contacto…`).
  - `log del servidor` is an anglicism where the platform's own es-ES says `registro del servidor` (`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/es-ES.metadata-forms.generated.ts:370`).
  - Better: `En este momento no se pueden imprimir registros en un archivo: el motor de impresión no está listo. El motivo figura en el registro del servidor.`
  - `es-ES.print_timed_out` `…en un archivo en el tiempo permitido para una impresión.` has a doubled `en`. Better: `No se pudo imprimir el registro en un archivo dentro del tiempo permitido.`
- N4 — The pin titled "…the cause in the fault log only" (`print-routes.test.ts`) asserts neither the fault-log line nor that `posture read failed at /srv/secret` is absent from the body. The same goes for the three zh-CN pins, whose throwers also carry `/srv/secret`. Add `expect(JSON.stringify(zh.body)).not.toContain('/srv/secret')`, or retitle the pin.
- N5 — 维护者速读's first bullet names three failure kinds (引擎未就绪、超时、服务器出错). The PR also localizes the caller-resolution 500, which the changeset and body do name.
- Landing: the zone lands it after measuring K; if K ≥ 15 it merges main first; a merge-only head move keeps this ACCEPT.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3dfbfdb5a135338fd76d80ceab81442c2315d4df`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/services/service-print/src/print-routes.ts, packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.test.ts, packages/services/service-print/src/print-routes.test.ts, .changeset/37260-print-failure-locale.md
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37272, card #37260. Read-only: the diff `origin/main...3dfbfdb5a` (6 files, +236 −12), the card thread with seat direction A, and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built or run locally. The remainder of the diff (`packages/services/service-print/vitest.config.ts`, a source alias for `@objectstack/spec/system`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What the catalog is.** `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` is a published export of `@objectstack/spec/system`, typed `Record<string, Record<string, string>>`. It is platform text, not authorable metadata: its own header says it ships as constants and stays out of the extract-and-gate bundle pipeline.
- **What reads its keys.** At head: `renderOperationMessage` (spec), `operationUserMessage` (`packages/core/src/utils/operation-user-message.ts`, which takes `messageKey: string`), plugin-security's locale probe, and producers that name a key literally. No client reads a key: the only `ui/` hit for an existing key name is a comment in `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`. No docs generator lists the keys: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` names two `errors.delete_restricted*` addresses by hand and nothing else.
- **Exported types and snapshots.** The value's type does not change, and no key union is exported. `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json` and `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json` record the const by name only, and the diff touches neither. No generated reference doc or JSON schema is in the diff. The head's `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness` and `Type Check · consumer gates` are all `success`, so no generated artifact drifted.
- **`Clause-②: no` is correct.** The test is whether the card widens an accepted set or enlarges the public surface. There is no new export, no type change and no new envelope member. `Accept-Language` was already an accepted header on this door. Four more entries in an existing exported record are data under an unchanged type. The earlier catalog changeset that called itself a widening did so for its new `operationUserMessage` export, which this PR only calls.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.** No key, value or metadata type an author can write is added, removed or changed in meaning. A `translation` item could always carry an `errors.print_*` key (the namespace is free-form), and its effect is the same before and after: none, see the nit under ④.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-print` is right. The kind is `none`, which takes `patch`; a non-protocol change ships `patch` either way. Both moved packages are named, and both declaration lines are line-initial in the changeset body and the PR body. `@objectstack/core` is called, not changed, so it is correctly absent. `Check Changeset` is `success` at this head. The changeset body's claims were each checked against code:
- "Code, status and the English text do not change": `sendServerFault` receives the same `status` and `code` arguments, and `print-routes.test.ts` L432–L438 and L458 pin the English against literal pre-change sentences.
- "the `/actions` door forwards the caller's `Accept-Language`": `accept-language` is on the forward allowlist at `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` L1451.
- "relays the door's `message` as written": the `forward-refused` arm of `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts` (L920–L931) relays an enveloped refusal whole. Read, not reviewed (outside the diff).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's open question (which envelope channel) is answered** by seat direction A on #37260, and the code agrees with both governing texts. The `sendServerFault` docblock (`packages/types/src/response-envelope.ts` L252–L254) says the wire carries `message`, the route's generic text, and nothing of `thrown`: the localized sentence is still that authored generic text, and `thrown` still goes only to the log. The actions-door fault exit (`packages/types/src/actions-door-answer.ts` L311–L315) says a fault's `userMessage` does not ride the exit: the PR adds none.
- **Out-of-scope findings** (the `/actions` forward-unavailable 503, the print bridge 501, the door's English 4xx refusals) are routed to a follow-up card by the seat. None is in this diff.
- **Bounded in-place fix** (`print_caller_unresolved`): same file, same class, pinned in zh-CN and with the header absent. Accepted as declared.
- **SQL push-down:** not applicable. The diff adds no query, id materialisation or join.
- **Security:** the diff changes the language of four authored sentences. It changes no permission, authentication or disclosure behaviour: the catalog test refuses wire codes, `Chromium`, `OS_PRINT` and any `/` in all 16 strings, so no host or engine vocabulary reaches the wire.

### ④ Design judgment

**`operation-message.ts` against direction A and its first consumer.**
- Key names follow the catalog's convention: `snake_case`, one key per situation and not per wire code. Two keys share `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` (`print_failed`, `print_caller_unresolved`), which is the header's own rule (#7451).
- Placeholder shape: none of the 16 strings takes a `{{name}}` placeholder, the header says so, and the test asserts it per locale. That matches the three other placeholder-free keys.
- All four locales define all four keys, so the `en` must-define-every-key rule holds and no locale falls through for a key another one carries.
- The header paragraph states what these keys are: the `message` of a 5xx, where every earlier member is a refusal's user sentence. That is a new kind of member, and it is documented at the seat rather than left implicit.
- The zh-CN strings use full-width punctuation throughout, as the catalog's zh-CN entries do.

**`print-routes.ts` against the contract it implements.**
- The envelope is unchanged: `success: false`, `error.code`, `error.message`, same status. An English request, an absent header, and a language the catalog lacks all read the pre-change bytes (pinned for 503, 504 and 500, and for `de-DE`).
- No console or SDK code matches on the sentence text: the only literal copies at head are the catalog and the two test files. Clients key on `code` and status, which do not move.
- `serverAnswerKeyFor` returns a literal union of three keys that exist in every locale, so a missing-key render cannot occur.
- The 4xx relay keeps the producer's text under `zh-CN` (pinned), so the change is confined to the door's own 5xx sentences, as the card asks.
- The dev's ablation (hard-coded English restored: 4 red, the English controls green) shows the new pins bind to the rendering line. It is the dev's run, cited from the PR body, not re-run here.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; candidates for the follow-up card, not for this PR):
- **Override address.** `operationMessageTranslationKey`'s docblock says a `translation` item defining `errors.KEY` overrides the built-in text.
